name: Ira
overview: Ira was a male warrior known as the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite and was counted as the eleventh member among "the thirty," an elite group of David's men. He held a position of military leadership, being in charge of the sixth division as recorded in the chronicles. His tribal affiliation is not specified in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Ira is a proper name which possibly means "stallion donkey." There is no indication that this name was given by God, but it identifies him distinctly among David's warriors.
familyAndRelationships: Ira is explicitly identified as the son of Ikkesh. Beyond this paternal relationship, Scripture does not record any other family relationships for him.
scriptureSignificance: Ira's significance lies in his role as a trusted warrior within King David's elite fighting force, "the thirty." His leadership over the sixth division highlights his responsibility and standing within David's military organization. As a member of this distinguished group, Ira contributed to the security and expansion of David's kingdom.
